_meta.what: Every test that is EXPECTED to fail right now, why, and which phase fixes it.
_meta.why: A baseline with 8 red tests is useless if you have to remember which 8 are fine. run_baseline.py marks a failure listed here as KNOWN and anything else as NEW - so only new failures demand attention. If a KNOWN test starts PASSING, it is reported too: either the fix landed, or the test got lucky (check with run_consistency.py).
_meta.how_to_update: When a phase fixes an issue, delete its entry here. When triage finds a new real bug, add it with the phase that will fix it. 'match' is a substring of the promptfoo test description.

issues.issue: FLAKY (step 1.7: loop in 1 of 3 runs). When it goes wrong, the Shift trend answer falls into a repetition loop (same alarm listed 46x), hits the 800-token cap and stops mid-sentence with no notice. The other 2 runs were good: they found the three alarm clusters (Jan, May, Jun).
issues.fix: Tighter shift prompt / repetition control; surface truncation on /ask.

issues.issue: Docs answer to 'what must be done after replacing the liner' omits 'instability in the first 5 minutes is expected, not a fault'. The warning only surfaces when the operator already names the symptom (G2-010 passes; retrieval rank 8).
issues.fix: Structure-aware chunking; experiment: store 'questions this chunk answers' for search.

issues.issue: CAUSE MOVED after the Phase 1B graph rebuild. The graph now offers the defective-spool cause correctly and a hand-run report named it. But an unreviewed operator capture ('wire tension 18 -> 22 units', numbers that appear in NO document) outranks it about half the time. In the failing run the report even quoted the SOP's 'Do NOT keep adjusting tension' as a contradiction and still made tension the root cause. FLAKY.
issues.fix: Precedence rule: an operator capture that contradicts a documented warning or whose numbers appear in no document may be surfaced, but must not be adopted as the root cause. Same family as the disputed-value rule added in Phase 1B, extended from numbers to actions.

issues.issue: Expected burn-in stutter rated HIGH and treated as a liner fault ('remove and reinstall liner').
issues.fix: Prompt rule 'LOTO needed = HIGH' must not override 'burn-in is expected'.

issues.issue: 3+ overload alarms per shift: answer gives SOP generic steps incl. 'adjust drive-roll tension' - the trap NCR-2024-047 warns against. Retrieval ranked the NCR lesson FIRST (step 1.5), so the AI ignored what it was given.
issues.fix: Prompt: when an NCR lesson applies, it overrides generic SOP steps.

issues.issue: FLAKY SAFETY RATING (step 1.7): parts welded with low shielding gas rated HIGH, HIGH, CRITICAL over 3 runs - correct only 1 in 3. The earlier single-run PASS was luck. A pass in any one run proves nothing; judge over several runs.
issues.fix: Take this rating away from the model: a code rule 'shielding gas low alarm => CRITICAL' as a floor, the same way work-order cost is computed in Python so the model cannot get it wrong.
